---
title: "Teaching"
---

I teach real estate and built-environment courses at the University of Denver,
with an emphasis on **social justice and environmental sustainability in the
built environment**. My classes lean on discussion-based learning to help
students engage deeply with the material, and I use classroom technology to give
students the chance to share their work with the world.

## Courses {#sec-courses}

### REAL 1700 / 4000 — Triple Bottom Line and the Built Environment

A topics course (formerly *Business of the Built Environment*) examining the
environmental, social, and economic dimensions of real estate and city building.

### REAL 3307 / 4407 — Real Estate Finance / Income Property Finance

Finance and investment analysis for income-producing real estate.

### REAL 4800 — NAIOP Rocky Mountain Real Estate Challenge

A capstone, competition-based course in which student teams develop a real
proposal for the regional NAIOP Real Estate Challenge.

### REAL 4701 — Real Estate Market Analysis

Methods for analyzing real estate markets, demand, and submarket dynamics.

---

## Student projects {#sec-student-projects}

In **Triple Bottom Line and the Built Environment**, students build public
websites around their work:

- **Graduate (REAL 4000).** Students choose a critical issue related to the built
  environment, outline the primary challenges, discuss how the issue affects the
  City of Denver, and propose a plan of action for Denver to address it.
- **Undergraduate (REAL 1700).** Students identify a parcel of land in the Denver
  metro region and propose a redevelopment — a regenerative feasibility study
  covering stakeholder engagement, a theoretical LEED rating, and the financing of
  green enhancements.

## Community-engaged scholarship {#sec-community}

The University of Denver is a private university committed to the public good. I
co-led the **Environmental Sustainability in an Urban Context** cohort of the DU
Grand Challenges, and I take part in the **Community Integrated Research Center
(CIRC)** — part of the CityCraft initiative bringing Front Range scholars together
to help the City and County of Denver redevelop West Denver in a regenerative way.

A few resources I point students and collaborators toward:

- [DU Center for Community Engagement to advance Scholarship and Learning (CCESL)](https://www.du.edu/ccesl/) — resources on community-engaged scholarship and learning.
- [DU Scholar Shop](https://duscholarshop.com/) — community partners interested in working with DU faculty and students.
- [Metro Denver Nature Alliance](https://www.metrodna.org/) — a coalition aligning nature-based efforts for more equitable access to nature.
